wy_mondo_beyondo.blurb: Mondo Beyondo is a collection of sport crags in the upper part of Ten Sleep Canyon in the Big Horns of Wyoming. Every climb here is a sport route, and most fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with a thin band of easier routes and a few at 5.13. Across the canyon, expect pockets, edges and flakes with kindly spaced bolts. At Downpour Wall, the steep face looks due south and tends to stay reasonably cool year round, and Slavery Wall sits under a large square roof. Downpour Wall holds the most climbs, followed by Metropolis, Frat Boys and World Domination.

az_sedona_bouldering.blurb: Sedona's bouldering lies near the banks of Oak Creek in northern Arizona, on steel-grey, featured sandstone. All of the climbing is bouldering, with problems from V0 and below up to V11. Most fall between V0 and V5, and there is a smaller group of harder problems around V9. The Anvil Boulders sit at the north end of town off the highway, on solid sandstone that suits the cooler shoulder season. Climbers here use cold-weather days on warm stone, and summer bouldering by the creek. The Anvil Boulders and Grasshopper Point Boulders hold the most climbs, followed by Upper Midgley Wash.

ca_land_of_the_lost_3.blurb: Land of the Lost is a cluster of quartzite crags tucked into the gullies and ridges of Horse Mountain in northwest California, reached east of Arcata through mature forest with wide views of the Trinity Alps. Sport climbing leads, with a fair amount of trad and a few boulder problems and top-ropes. Routes are typically 40 to 80 feet tall and most grade between 5.10 and 5.12, with some moderates in the 5.6 to 5.9 range. Spring through fall is the main season, since winter brings snow. Pinch Me Wall has plenty of moderates, while Tropics Wall and Three Amigos Wall draw climbers at 5.11 and 5.12. The Glory Hole is mostly shaded through the day.
